valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E (FY2027 adjusted diluted EPS viewed at the 12-month target date)

bear.driver: Tariff/macro headwinds, EV margin drag, and cyclical multiple compression

base.driver: Steady North America truck/SUV pricing, $20B buyback reducing share count (849M shares as of 2026-09-30), and modest multiple expansion

bull.driver: Stronger margin resilience, faster OnStar/software and GM Defense scaling, and index/listing re-rating

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY2027 EPS of $14.50, the $86.00 close implies 5.93x forward P/E; the $96-$132 named analyst target range implies 6.62x to 9.10x (or $14.77 to $20.31 EPS at 6.5x).
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $14.50 (16.9 pp of return).
valuation.watch_metric: FY2027 EBIT-adjusted, North America net pricing and incentive trends, and share repurchase pace.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 2026 and full-year 2026 earnings release (expected January 27, 2027).

analyst_notes: Following GM's Q3 2026 earnings release on October 20, 2026 (adjusted EPS $3.70, narrowed FY2026 EPS guidance $12.75-$13.75), several analysts trimmed targets (UBS to $109, Barclays to $105, Goldman Sachs to $96, RBC to $98) while maintaining Buy/Overweight/Outperform ratings. Named targets ($96-$132) sit above the $94.25 base case (+9.6% upside), reflecting higher assumed multiples (6.6x-9.1x vs. 6.5x) or faster ancillary growth in OnStar and GM Defense.
